title: Implement and manage physical security: decision comparison 1
teachingQuestion: At which physical boundary should a control prevent, detect, or record access/environmental harm, and who must respond?
focalInsight: Boundary, authorization, zone separation, monitoring, environmental protection, and compensating control for a failed device.
caption: Compare meaning, decision conditions, and failures. These concise distinctions are paired with the worked examples in the teaching unit.

nodes.label: Physical Security
nodes.definition: The coordinated protection of people, facilities, equipment, media, and environmental conditions through physical layers and operations.
nodes.decision: Select layered controls from asset value, threat, safety, privacy, and operational need; assign monitoring and response ownership.
nodes.failureExample: Installing devices with no monitoring or maintenance produces an appearance of protection, not a working control.
nodes.detail: The coordinated protection of people, facilities, equipment, media, and environmental conditions through physical layers and operations.

nodes.label: Perimeter Control
nodes.definition: Control at or approaching the property/building boundary that channels, deters, detects, or restricts entry and movement.
nodes.decision: Use where the organization needs early detection or managed approach before access to the facility interior.
nodes.failureExample: A perimeter with unmonitored gaps moves confrontation and detection closer to protected assets.
nodes.detail: Control at or approaching the property/building boundary that channels, deters, detects, or restricts entry and movement.

nodes.label: Perimeter Security Controls
nodes.definition: The set of outer-boundary measures such as barriers, lighting, gates, exterior entry controls, cameras, and intrusion sensors.
nodes.decision: Layer controls so approach detection, delay, identification, and response suit the site threat and safety conditions.
nodes.failureExample: Relying only on a fence without detection or response leaves a breach unnoticed.
nodes.detail: The set of outer-boundary measures such as barriers, lighting, gates, exterior entry controls, cameras, and intrusion sensors.

nodes.label: Entry Control
nodes.definition: The authorization and controlled flow of people or materials through a defined entrance, using methods such as badges, guards, locks, or visitor procedures.
nodes.decision: Match identity assurance and escort requirements to the area’s risk while preserving safe emergency egress.
nodes.failureExample: A locked door with informal tailgating defeats the authorization decision it is meant to enforce.
nodes.detail: The authorization and controlled flow of people or materials through a defined entrance, using methods such as badges, guards, locks, or visitor procedures.

nodes.label: Internal Security Controls
nodes.definition: Controls inside the facility that restrict and monitor movement among rooms, zones, racks, media areas, and sensitive operations.
nodes.decision: Use internal layers to enforce need-to-access after someone legitimately enters the building.
nodes.failureExample: Treating lobby access as permission for a server room enables lateral physical movement.
nodes.detail: Controls inside the facility that restrict and monitor movement among rooms, zones, racks, media areas, and sensitive operations.

nodes.label: Security Zone
nodes.definition: A physically bounded area with a defined asset sensitivity, authorized population, entry conditions, and monitoring/response rules.
nodes.decision: Create zones where access requirements change; document transitions and exceptions.
nodes.failureExample: An undefined “secure area” leaves staff unable to enforce who may enter or escort visitors.
nodes.detail: A physically bounded area with a defined asset sensitivity, authorized population, entry conditions, and monitoring/response rules.

nodes.label: Cctv
nodes.definition: Closed-circuit video surveillance used to observe, deter, investigate, or verify activity in a defined field of view.
nodes.decision: Place and secure cameras for needed coverage, privacy limits, recording availability, and response use; protect IP-connected cameras as systems.
nodes.failureExample: A camera pointed away from the entry or with unavailable recording cannot corroborate a tailgating event.
nodes.detail: Closed-circuit video surveillance used to observe, deter, investigate, or verify activity in a defined field of view.

nodes.label: Intrusion Detection
nodes.definition: Sensors and alarms that identify unauthorized boundary or zone entry attempts, such as door, motion, beam, vibration, or gate sensors.
nodes.decision: Choose sensing appropriate to the environment and connect it to monitored triage and escalation.
nodes.failureExample: A motion sensor with no alarm response only records a problem after the intruder has acted.
nodes.detail: Sensors and alarms that identify unauthorized boundary or zone entry attempts, such as door, motion, beam, vibration, or gate sensors.

nodes.label: Environmental Control
nodes.definition: Physical safeguards that maintain conditions or limit hazards affecting people and equipment, including fire, HVAC, water, and power protections.
nodes.decision: Select controls from environmental hazards and life-safety requirements, with facilities and emergency coordination.
nodes.failureExample: An equipment room can remain access-controlled yet fail from heat, smoke, or water.
nodes.detail: Physical safeguards that maintain conditions or limit hazards affecting people and equipment, including fire, HVAC, water, and power protections.

learningContract.teachingQuestion: At which physical boundary should a control prevent, detect, or record access/environmental harm, and who must respond?
learningContract.misconception: A camera, badge reader, or sensor protects an asset by itself.
learningContract.formRationale: Aligned columns make concept meanings, decision criteria and failure consequences explicit and comparable.
learningContract.focalInsight: Boundary, authorization, zone separation, monitoring, environmental protection, and compensating control for a failed device.
learningContract.intentionalOmissions: Do not prescribe a universal device model, retention duration, guard staffing level, or building code requirement.
learningContract.retrievalPrompt: A visitor tailgates into a server corridor while a door sensor is offline. Identify the boundary, missed control, compensating measure, and evidence needed.
